name: StreamForce
description: StreamForce (Streaming Video Generation with Streaming Force Control) is a causal, unified framework for real-time streaming video generation developed by Northeastern University (NEU-VI Lab). It enables physically grounded interactive control over video rollouts via continuous, time-varying force inputs at up to 16.6 FPS.
keyFeatures: Physically Grounded Streaming Control: Accepts continuous time-varying force vectors to dynamically manipulate video streams
Causal Autoregressive Architecture: Generates video sequentially from an initial image frame for low-latency interactive steerability
Real-Time Speed (up to 16.6 FPS): Efficient force-controllable distillation pipeline enables streaming generation on a single GPU
Unified Force Signal Representation: Combines local impulses and global environmental forces into a unified control signal space
Physical & Photometric Realism: Maintains object persistence and motion plausibility under interactive user force interventions
curatorNotes: Verified research paper arXiv:2606.07508 from Northeastern University (NEU-VI Lab). Code repository announced on GitHub.
